newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Camelot says Were ends underwriting deal.
newsitem.headline: Camelot says Were ends underwriting deal.

text.p: Gold miner Camelot Resources NL said on Monday it would now seek to retain a stake of only 30 percent in the Mt Edon assets in Western Australia following the slump in the gold price and the termination of an underwriting agreement by broker J.B. Were and Son.

The broker was to have underwritten in full a A$34.9 million rights issue but exercised its right to terminate the agreement due to the fall in the Australian Gold Index below 1,340 points, the company said.
Camelot hoped to acquire a 50 percent stake in Mt Edon, funded by the rights issue and a A$25 million note issue.

"The recent fall in the gold price and the resultant difficult conditions in worldwide gold equity markets have brought tremendous pressure to bear on Camelot's efforts to raise capital to refinance its stake in the former Mt Edon assets," the company said.
Mt Edon Gold Mines (Australia) Ltd was recently acquired by Reachwest, a company jointly owned by Camelot and Canada's Teck Corp.
Camelot said its interest in Mt Edon had been funded by cash resources and a bridging finance facility.

"In order for Camelot to repay its share of the bridging facility and retain its share of the Mt Edon assets, Camelot must contribute a further A$32.5 million to retain 30 percent ownership or A$59.1 million to retain a 50 percent stake under its agreement with Teck Corp," the company said.

Camelot said it would seek to retain the 30 percent stake at a cost of A$32.5 million, with the funds to be raised by a rights issue underwritten by Teck Corp that would seek to raise at least A$22 million and a convertible note issue to raise A$10 million. It said the note issue would be underwritten by a Swiss-based fund manager GHP Financial Services AG.

Teck Corp would have a 43.7 percent stake in Camelot if the Canadian company subscribed to the full amount of its underwriting commitment, with Camelot to issue Teck 25 million options in substitution of a cash underwriting fee.
Mt Edon operates the Tarmoola mine and has exploration properties around the town of Leonora.
